findings.issue_text: [Medium/data] lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13 — `BlockedEmail.should_block?` performs a database write (increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, saves) as a side effect of validation; validations run on every `valid?`/`save` where `email_changed?`, so repeated validation inflates match statistics and issues writes inside whatever transaction wraps the save

[Medium/bug] app/models/blocked_email.rb:11 — `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact case-sensitive match, so a blocked `bad@spam.com` is bypassed by `Bad@Spam.com`; neither the lookup nor the uniqueness validation normalizes case. Downcase on write and lookup or use a `lower(email)` comparison

[Medium/security] lib/validators/email_validator.rb:19-21 — Domain restriction regex `@(domains)` is not anchored at the end (whitelist `example.com` lets `user@example.com.attacker.net` pass; blacklist `spam.com` blocks `user@spam.com.example.org`) and only `.` is escaped, so other regex metacharacters in the site setting are interpreted; re-created from removed `User#email_in_restriction_setting?` without fixing. Add `$`/`\z` anchoring and `Regexp.escape` per domain

[Low/concurrency] app/models/blocked_email.rb:13-15 — Read-modify-write of `match_count` (`record.match_count += 1; record.save`) is not atomic; concurrent registrations against the same blocked email lose increments. Use an atomic `update_all` or `increment_counter`

[Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:17 — `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is defined on the class prototype, so the same array instance is shared across all `CreateAccountController` instances instead of being per-instance state; initialize in `init` or via a computed property

[Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:275 — Client stores `result.values.email` (server-side attribute) and compares with `contains(email)` against `accountEmail` (what the user typed); if the model normalizes the email (strip/downcase) before validation the strings differ and the rejected-email check never fires

[Low/bug] lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13 — `should_block?` is only invoked when no domain-restriction error was added, so a blocked email on a blacklisted/non-whitelisted domain never has its `match_count`/`last_match_at` updated, leaving the stats the model spec asserts on incomplete

[Low/test_gap] spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb — Only the blocked-email branch is tested with `should_block?` stubbed; no coverage for the whitelist/blacklist branches now in this validator, no test that `User` validation surfaces `user.email.blocked` end-to-end, and no controller spec asserting the new `errors`/`values` keys in the `users#create` failure response the JS depends on

[Low/api] app/controllers/users_controller.rb:198-199 — Failure response adds `errors` and `values` keys, but the JS treats presence of `result.errors.email` as a permanent rejection cached client-side for the session; transient email errors (e.g. uniqueness) then show as `user.email.invalid` with no way to retry without reloading, and the specific server reason (`blocked`, `not_allowed`) is discarded for a generic invalid message

goldens.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/concurrency] app/models/blocked_email.rb:13-15 — Read-modify-write of `match_count` (`record.match_count += 1; record.save`) is not atomic; concurrent registrations against the same blocked email lose increments. Use an atomic `update_all` or `increment_counter`

adjudication.rationale: In `BlockedEmail.should_block?` (new file `app/models/blocked_email.rb`), the code does a read-modify-write (`record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = ...; record.save`). Under concurrent calls for the same `email`, two processes can read the same `match_count` and both write back `+1`, losing an increment (and possibly last_match_at ordering). This is a real concurrency/data-correctness defect in the stats tracking introduced by this diff; an atomic `update_all`/`increment_counter`-style update would avoid lost updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:17 — `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is defined on the class prototype, so the same array instance is shared across all `CreateAccountController` instances instead of being per-instance state; initialize in `init` or via a computed property

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` as a plain property on the `Discourse.CreateAccountController = Discourse.Controller.extend(...)` definition. In Ember, object/array literals (and objects created at class definition time) on `extend` become prototype properties, so the same `Em.A([])` instance can be shared across controller instances. Since the diff also mutates it (`get('rejectedEmails').pushObject(...)`), rejected emails can leak between instances/uses of the controller, causing incorrect validation behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:275 — Client stores `result.values.email` (server-side attribute) and compares with `contains(email)` against `accountEmail` (what the user typed); if the model normalizes the email (strip/downcase) before validation the strings differ and the rejected-email check never fires

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a client-side cache `rejectedEmails` and checks `rejectedEmails.contains(email)` where `email` is `accountEmail` (user input), but on failure it stores `result.values.email` returned from the server (`pushObject(result.values.email)`). This is strict string matching, so any discrepancy between what the server echoes back (e.g., normalized casing/whitespace) and what the user typed would bypass the rejection shortcut. The diff doesn’t show any normalization, so it’s not a verifiable defect here, but it is a concrete robustness issue created by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13 — `should_block?` is only invoked when no domain-restriction error was added, so a blocked email on a blacklisted/non-whitelisted domain never has its `match_count`/`last_match_at` updated, leaving the stats the model spec asserts on incomplete

adjudication.rationale: In `EmailValidator#validate_each`, `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` is gated by `record.errors[attribute].blank?` (line with `and BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`), so if a whitelist/blacklist restriction already added an error, `should_block?` will not be called and thus `match_count`/`last_match_at` won’t be updated for those attempts. This is real and grounded in the diff, but it affects statistics/telemetry completeness rather than correctness of validation (the email is already rejected), and the provided specs don’t assert this cross-condition behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb — Only the blocked-email branch is tested with `should_block?` stubbed; no coverage for the whitelist/blacklist branches now in this validator, no test that `User` validation surfaces `user.email.blocked` end-to-end, and no controller spec asserting the new `errors`/`values` keys in the `users#create` failure response the JS depends on

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial new behavior and API surface without corresponding coverage: `lib/validators/email_validator.rb` now contains whitelist/blacklist logic (copied from the removed `User#email_validator`) plus the new `BlockedEmail.should_block?` branch, but `spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb` only exercises the blocked-email path with `should_block?` stubbed and does not cover the whitelist/blacklist branches. Additionally, `users_controller.rb#create` now returns new JSON keys `errors` and `values`, and `create_account_controller.js` depends on `result.errors.email` and `result.values.email` to populate `rejectedEmails`, but the diff adds no controller/request spec asserting those keys are present on failure. These are concrete, diff-grounded test gaps rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] app/controllers/users_controller.rb:198-199 — Failure response adds `errors` and `values` keys, but the JS treats presence of `result.errors.email` as a permanent rejection cached client-side for the session; transient email errors (e.g. uniqueness) then show as `user.email.invalid` with no way to retry without reloading, and the specific server reason (`blocked`, `not_allowed`) is discarded for a generic invalid message

adjudication.rationale: In `create_account_controller.js`, any failed create response with `result.errors.email` causes `result.values.email` to be pushed into `rejectedEmails` (new array state). The `emailValidation` computed property now short-circuits when `rejectedEmails.contains(email)` and returns a hardcoded failure reason `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')`, discarding the server-provided email error details (`blocked`, `not_allowed`, uniqueness, etc.). This makes that email permanently invalid for the remainder of the session (until reload) regardless of whether the server-side condition was transient, and it replaces specific server reasons with a generic message.
